boards.title: Your First Weekend at Johns Hopkins University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe first-weekend loop through Homewood campus and its immediate cultural neighbor, with each stop offering a clear next move.

cards.title: Start with a campus bearing
cards.subtitle: Homewood Campus lawn
cards.notes: Begin outdoors with a short pause on the grass, then use the surrounding paths to orient yourself before choosing your next campus stop.
cards.short_summary: An easy first landmark for getting your bearings on Homewood.
cards.evidence_claim: Johns Hopkins identifies The Beach as a Homewood campus area where people can spread out a blanket, read, hang out, or people-watch.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus area; follow any posted campus access rules.

cards.title: Find the clock tower
cards.subtitle: Homewood Campus humanities building
cards.notes: Walk to Gilman and use its clock tower as a visual waypoint. Check the building’s public areas and posted access guidance before going inside.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus landmark that helps anchor a first walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Johns Hopkins describes Gilman Hall as one of Homewood’s oldest buildings, home to the humanities, an archaeological museum, and a clock tower.
cards.source_title: Our Network of Campuses | Johns Hopkins University Admissions
cards.access_notes: Building access may vary; observe posted entry requirements.

cards.title: Settle into Brody
cards.subtitle: Homewood Campus library commons
cards.notes: Take a quiet reset in the reading room or choose a seat for planning. Bring your J-Card in case campus access controls are in effect.
cards.short_summary: A practical indoor pause between exploring campus and making plans.
cards.evidence_claim: Brody Learning Commons connects to Eisenhower Library and includes a quiet reading room, 16 group study rooms, teaching rooms, and a café.
cards.access_notes: Sheridan Libraries lists Brody as open 24/7; temporary access restrictions may apply.

cards.title: Look for a campus program
cards.subtitle: Between The Beach and Brody Learning Commons
cards.notes: Stop by to check the current program board, student-organization activity, or shared spaces; choose a public event only if it fits your schedule.
cards.short_summary: A central place to see what student life is offering that weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: JHU says the Bloomberg Student Center sits between The Beach and Brody and can host club meetings and campus events.
cards.source_title: Visit the Bloomberg Student Center | JHU Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Programs and building access vary; consult the current center schedule.

cards.title: Pause in Levering Hall
cards.subtitle: Homewood Campus student gathering space
cards.notes: Use the hall as a midday meeting point, then check current campus listings for an open movie, craft class, or other student program.
cards.short_summary: A longstanding campus gathering place with food and event space nearby.
cards.evidence_claim: JHU Admissions identifies Levering Hall as a place for lunch, coffee, study sessions, movie nights, DIY crafting classes, and other events.
cards.source_title: Our Network of Campuses | Johns Hopkins University Admissions
cards.access_notes: Food and programs may require payment, registration, or current building access.

cards.title: Make an art-gallery detour
cards.subtitle: 10 Art Museum Drive, beside Homewood
cards.notes: Reserve a free general-admission ticket, then give yourself time for the permanent galleries. Confirm any special-exhibition ticket requirements before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A nearby museum visit with free general admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The Baltimore Museum of Art states that general admission is always free, with a free ticket reservation required for gallery entry.
cards.access_notes: General galleries are Wednesday–Sunday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m., with Thursday hours until 9 p.m.; reserve a free ticket.

cards.title: Tour Homewood Museum
cards.subtitle: Homewood Campus historic house museum
cards.notes: Book a docent tour in advance or choose the self-guided audio option during open hours. Leave time to look closely at the period rooms.
cards.short_summary: A focused historic-house stop directly on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: JHU Museums lists self-guided audio tours during open hours and docent-guided tours by advance reservation; period rooms are included with tour admission.
cards.source_title: Homewood Museum Visitor Information | JHU Museums
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Tuesday–Sunday, 11 a.m.–4 p.m.; tour admission applies, while the Housekeeper’s Room can be viewed without admission.

cards.entity_name: Ralph S. O’Connor Center for Recreation and Well-Being
cards.title: Move at the Rec Center
cards.subtitle: Homewood Campus recreation facility
cards.notes: If you have an active student membership, check the recreation calendar and choose an available fitness, climbing, or court activity that suits your group.
cards.short_summary: A membership-based option for a more active weekend stop.
cards.evidence_claim: JHU states that the O’Connor Center offers memberships to students and that a membership application must be completed before entering.
cards.access_notes: Active membership and a completed application are required before entry; it is not open to the general community for membership.

cards.title: Catch a Blue Jays home game
cards.subtitle: Homewood Campus athletics venue
cards.notes: Check the current athletics schedule, then attend a home competition with friends and use the walk back across campus to compare weekend plans.
cards.short_summary: A campus-based spectator option when a home competition is scheduled.
cards.evidence_claim: JHU Student Well-Being states that all Hopkins home athletics competitions, including lacrosse, are free for students and held on the Homewood campus.
cards.source_title: Why joining “The Flock” is good for your health | JHU Student Well-Being
cards.access_notes: Only applicable when a home competition is scheduled; the cited free entry applies to JHU students.

cards.title: End on Freshman Quad
cards.subtitle: Homewood Campus quad
cards.notes: Use the quad as a final outdoor meet-up point, then make a simple plan for the week ahead before heading back to your residence or next event.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable Homewood gathering point for a relaxed weekend wrap-up.
cards.evidence_claim: JHU Student Affairs identifies Freshman Quad as the location for campus activities including its Well-Being Day programming.
cards.source_title: Well-Being Day 2024 | Johns Hopkins University Student Well-Being
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; availability can change for scheduled programs or maintenance.
